title: Incomplete moulting gives Estheria a mollusc-like spiral shell with growth lines

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Incomplete moulting gives Estheria a mollusc-like spiral shell with growth lines

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: The bivalved carapace of the crustacean Estheria resembles a lamellibranch shell, with lines of growth and a logarithmic spiral of small angle, because its moult is incomplete: each old carapace is retained and the new one grows beneath it and projects beyond its edge.

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: But in Estheria (and one or two other small crustacea) the moult is incomplete: the old carapace is retained, and the new, growing up underneath it, adheres to it like a lining, and projects beyond its edge: so that in course of time the margins of successive old carapaces appear as “lines of growth” upon the surface of the shell.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter XI, “The Logarithmic Spiral”; topic “Bivalve carapace of Estheria”. Scope: Estheria and similar conchostracan crustaceans

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch11-17: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.64

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Nested layers and spiral lines are measurable, and the mechanism has a useful comparative prediction. Public developmental coverage of the relevant clam-shrimp taxa is likely too sparse for full causal resolution.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Use developmental imaging and preserved carapaces to test whether successive retained exuviae adhere as nested layers, project beyond prior margins and generate fitted logarithmic growth lines. Comparison with fully moulting branchiopods would test the incomplete-moult mechanism.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Static carapaces may not distinguish retained moults from continuous secretion.

Estheria is a historical taxonomic name.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The outline spiral and the presence of marginal lines can be scored from museum photographs of a narrow group of crustaceans, which are present in public collections. The mechanism, incomplete moulting with a new carapace under the old one, is decided by cross-sections that are not assembled as a dataset. Photographs therefore test the mollusc-like geometry and only proxy the moult interpretation.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: On Estheria and similar conchostracans, test whether surface lines are edges of retained moults, visible in section as stacked carapaces, and whether the outline is a logarithmic spiral of small angle. Stacked retained valves support the incomplete-moult mechanism; a single accreted sheet with growth lines would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
External lines alone cannot separate retained moults from true shell accretion; that needs sections, which are mostly in papers.

Estheria has been split among several modern genera, so the specimen set has to be delimited carefully.
